classification: PAPER EXPERIMENTAL FRAMING FREEZE. Experimental protocol wording. Not PAPER-FAITHFUL. Does not invent results. Does not authorize new architectures.
decided_by: PI, 2026-10-01: Fully Shared+z+r is not 'just another baseline'; it is the shared/latent realization of the proposed framework. Rename parameter-sharing section accordingly.

Ours-Teachers.policy_family: Separated role composites: for each s in {A,B}, {pi_s,ATTACK, pi_s,DEFEND}

Ours-Shared.definition: Fully Shared+z+r := pi(a | o, z, r) distilled from sealed Ours-Teachers
Ours-Shared.role: shared latent-strategy realization of the proposed framework
Ours-Shared.not: a neutral comparison baseline treated like Share-Encoder

COMPARISON_SET_locked.tests: Reference: preserve teachers with no sharing pressure (same as Ours-Teachers at Stage 4 entry)
Baseline: how much sharing can happen before strategy changes?
Can one shared network preserve A/B as strategic modes?
Ablation: does removing z destroy the A/B distinction?

SECTION_NAMING_locked.inside_sentence: We compare a separated reference, a partially shared encoder, our fully shared strategy-conditioned representation (Ours-Shared), and a role-only ablation.

RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_locked.RQ1_Strategic_differentiation: Does the symmetric dual-branch method produce reproducibly different opponent-conditioned team strategies across 2v2, 4v4, and 6v6?
RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_locked.RQ2_Role_mechanism: Does explicit ATTACK/DEFEND organization create or preserve strategic distinctions that are absent or weaker in the no-role specialists?
RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_locked.RQ3_Shared_latent_representation: Can the strategies produced by the role-organized teachers be preserved inside a shared policy using an explicit strategic mode z and role r?
RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_locked.RQ4_Is_z_necessary: When role information r is retained but strategic mode z is removed, does the A/B strategic distinction collapse?
RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_locked.secondary: raw win rate and robustness are secondary analyses, not central contribution questions

PROGRESSION_locked: RQ1: Do A and B actually become different strategies?
RQ2: Did explicit organization help produce that distinction?
RQ3: Can those strategies survive sharing as latent modes?
RQ4: Does removing z specifically erase strategy?

EVIDENCE_MAP_locked.RQ1: Ours-Teachers A vs B: behavioral signatures + four-cell crossover; Delta is functional evidence, not the sole definition
EVIDENCE_MAP_locked.RQ2: No-Role Specialists vs Ours-Teachers (same role construction on A and B)
EVIDENCE_MAP_locked.RQ3: Separated -> Share-Encoder -> Ours-Shared (z+r) as a sharing ladder, not a win-rate horse race
EVIDENCE_MAP_locked.RQ4: pi(a|o,z,r) vs pi(a|o,r) under matched data, roles, budget, and eval

HOPEFUL_PATTERN_not_a_gate: Ours-Shared + z+r: retains distinction in one shared net
Role-only: loses or weakens A/B distinction
ALLOWED_OUTCOMES_still: Role-only also preserves A/B -> z may be unnecessary under these conditions
Ours-Shared also collapses -> aggressive sharing may destroy strategic structure
teachers never become behaviorally distinct -> Stage 4 cannot invent a distinction that is not there
HISTORICAL_TABLES: Old sealed Share-Encoder / Fully Shared+z / Generalist numbers remain provenance under asymmetric teachers. Do not relabel those historical Fully Shared+z rows as Ours-Shared.
NOT_AUTHORIZED: calling Ours-Shared a baseline in the live Stage 4 writeup
claiming confirmatory results before the dual-branch Stage 4 seals exist
reintroducing Generalist pi(a|o) as a Stage 4 rung
